findings.note: _discard_batch swallows a journal unlink failure without reporting whether deletion succeeded, while recovery at line 2058 unconditionally treats an all-PRE/all-POST journal as resolved and proceeds. The still-live journal can therefore remain while a fresh publication changes its targets; the next scan then classifies those targets as neither the old PRE nor POST generation and Blocks as unrecoverable. The same silent failure after a completed rollback can retain a journal whose Evidence target has already been replaced by the Block record. This violates the required delete-then-proceed/Complete semantics and can turn a transient cleanup failure into persistent manual-intervention state.
